lesson.title: ar, ch, oo
lesson.html:
ar says /är/ (R-controlled vowel): car, garden.
ch says /ch/ (chair), /k/ (school), /sh/ (chef).
oo says /ö/ (moon), /ü/ (book), /ō/ (door).

lesson.title: Advanced phonogram bt
lesson.html: bt says /t/ in words from Latin: doubt, debt. The b is silent. We mark advanced phonograms with an A.

lesson.title: Sort the phonograms
lesson.html: Consonants: ch th ck ng sh qu · Multi-letter vowels: ee ea ai ay oi oy oo · R-controlled vowels: ar or er

lesson.title: Schwa /ә/
lesson.html: A lazy vowel in an unstressed syllable or word: /ŭ/ or /ĭ/. Hand under your chin: the syllable that opens your mouth wider is stressed. Left journal page: human, gallon, basket, broken. Right page: the, a, was, of.

lesson.title: Rules 10 · 30 · 31.1
lesson.html: Rule 10 broad A: ball, water. Rule 30 double F, L, S after a single vowel: cliff, full, glass. Rule 31.1 schwa in an unstressed syllable or word.

lesson.title: Noun · Adjective · Article
lesson.html: Find the noun first. An adjective tells what kind. A, an, the are article adjectives. a full moon = A Adj N.

lesson.title: Commas in a series
lesson.html: Two items: no comma (sun and moon). Three or more: commas + and — balls, cards, toys, and books.

lesson.title: Morphemes
lesson.html: pend = to hang · fend = to strike · part = separate · spect = to look · quart = four · plaint = lament

lesson.title: Compound words & suffixes
lesson.html: tooth + brush · class + room · fear + less · smooth + est · quart + er

list.q: What sound does the advanced phonogram bt say?
list.why: bt says /t/ — the b is silent.

list.q: bt says /t/ in words that came from…
list.why: doubt and debt came from Latin.

list.q: Which words have the phonogram bt?
What do we write above an advanced phonogram like bt?
list.why: Advanced phonograms are used less often, so we mark them with an A.

list.q: Finish the sentence: Do not ______ yourself.
Schwa is a lazy vowel sound. It sounds like…
Hand under your chin, say “morning.” Which syllable is stressed?
list.why: The syllable that opens your mouth wider is stressed: MOR-ning.
BAS-ket: the unstressed syllable is ket.

list.q: In “basket,” which vowel says the schwa sound?
list.why: The e in ket is lazy: bas-kәt.

list.q: Which words are unstressed (schwa) in “The cat sat on a chair”?
list.why: Small words like the and a are often unstressed.

list.q: True or false: a stressed syllable has a clearly pronounced vowel.
list.why: Stressed syllables have a clear vowel.

list.q: Spelling Journal: which page do you write “human” on?
list.why: Left page = unstressed syllable in a word with more than one syllable.

list.q: Spelling Journal: which page do you write “the” on?
list.why: Right page = a one-syllable unstressed word (the, a, was).

list.q: Which words go on the LEFT page?
list.why: Left: unstressed syllables in longer words (gallon, broken).

list.q: Which words go on the RIGHT page?
Which is the only word where F says /v/?
list.why: of is the only word where F says /v/.

list.q: What does the schwa symbol look like?
list.why: The schwa symbol ә looks like an upside-down e.

list.q: In “garden,” which syllable has the schwa?
Rule 10: A may say /ä/ after a ___ or before an ___
list.why: Broad A: after a W or before an L (water, ball).

list.q: Which two words have the broad /ä/?
Rule 30: we often double F, L and S after a single ______ at the end of a base word.
list.why: cliff, full, glass: double F, L, S after a single vowel.

list.q: Rule 31.1: any vowel may say a schwa sound in an unstressed ______ or unstressed ______.
list.why: Schwa lives in unstressed syllables and unstressed words.

list.q: Which rule: “double F, L and S”?

list.why: Rule 31.1: garden, human, the, a, was, of.

list.q: In “Mia told me a secret,” what is the word “secret”?
list.why: A secret is a thing — a noun.

list.q: In “The secret door is hidden,” what is the word “secret”?
list.why: Secret tells what kind of door — an adjective.

list.q: In “He drank a glass of milk,” what is “glass”?
list.why: A glass is a thing — a noun.

list.q: In “The glass jar broke,” what is “glass”?
list.why: Glass tells what kind of jar — an adjective.

list.why: Three or more items: a comma after each item before the last, and before the word and.

list.a: two cats, three dogs, and five ducks
w: two cats three dogs and five ducks
two cats, three dogs and, five ducks
two cats, three, dogs and five ducks
list.why: Commas separate the items; the comma goes before and.

list.a: red hats, blue socks, and green shoes
w: red hats blue socks and green shoes
red, hats blue, socks and green shoes
red hats, blue socks and, green shoes
list.why: Commas between the items in the series.
Comma after each item before the last.

w: red hats blue socks and green shoes
list.why: Only two items, so no comma.

list.q: Why is there no comma in “sun and moon”?
In a list of three or more, where does the comma go?
list.a: After each item before the last (before the word and)
list.why: toy cars, toy trains, and balls.
con = with, junct = to join, ion = noun suffix.

list.q: Circle the conjunction: the sun and the full moon
list.why: And joins the sun and the full moon.

list.q: Circle the conjunction: We saw ducks, geese, and swans.
list.why: And joins the last item to the list.

list.q: Circle the conjunction: Tom and Ava rode the bus.
The word “conjunction” = con + junct + ion. What does junct mean?

list.why: suspenders = sus- + pend + -er + -s: things that hang below.
classroom = class + room; bookmark = book + mark.
Two words join to make a new word.

list.q: A compound word is formed when two ______ join together to form a new ______.
Quart means four. So a quarter is one of ___ equal parts.
list.why: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts.
balloon = ball + -oon: it is round like a ball.

list.q: What was added to the end of “ball” to make “balloon”?
What sound does the A say in the first syllable of “balloon”?
list.why: The broad /ä/ in ball changes to schwa in balloon.

list.q: Why do we spell “balloon” with an A?
list.a: It is related to “ball” in meaning

list.q: A spectator is a person who ______ an event.

list.why: de- comes at the beginning: a prefix.

list.q: In “apartment,” a- is a form of the prefix…
list.why: a- is a form of ad- (to, toward, add).

list.q: Add -es to sandwich to make it plural.
list.why: Words that end in a hissing sound add -es.

list.q: Which is a word with the suffix -iff?

list.why: A pendant hangs on a chain.
